title: S&P 500 Forward P/E Hits 3-Year Low, but There's a Catch
summary: The S&P 500 forward P/E fell to 17.7 on Nov. 5, its lowest since 2023, per FactSet. Rising earnings estimates did the work, and that is the catch.
body_markdown:
Communication Services was the only sector with a negative aggregate surprise, with earnings 22.1% below estimates, led by Charter Communications,[Meta Platforms (META)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/meta/) and[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) , FactSet noted. Per the same report, Meta's GAAP results included a $9.89 billion litigation charge and Alphabet's an $8.7 billion loss on equity securities, and excluding those three companies would lift the index surprise to 6.7%.


Among the so-called Magnificent 7, Alphabet,[Amazon.com (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) and Meta reported negative EPS surprises for Q3 and saw an average price decline of 7.8% from two days before to two days after their releases, compared with an average 1.1% decline for all index companies with negative surprises, FactSet data show.


## Trailing P/E of 25.4 Stays Above Long-Term Averages


The forward ratio leans on analysts' estimates, so the trailing P/E, which uses actual reported profits, gives a second view. FactSet's Nov. 13 report put the trailing 12-month P/E at 25.4, above the 5-year average of 24.4 and the 10-year average of 23.7, while the forward P/E had moved back up to 18.3.


Measure Reading 5-year average 10-year average


Forward 12-month P/E, Nov. 5, 2026 17.7 19.8 19.1


Forward 12-month P/E, Nov. 13, 2026 report 18.3 19.8 19.1


Trailing 12-month P/E, Nov. 13, 2026 report 25.4 24.4 23.7


Source: FactSet Insight (Nov. 9, 2026) and FactSet Earnings Insight (Nov. 13, 2026).


That gap is the catch Adam Levy described in the Motley Fool article: the cheaper forward multiple holds up only if earnings keep growing at a high pace, and expectations are far higher than they were three years ago, which leaves more room for disappointment.


Levy noted that some see AI spending driving further growth, while others point to tighter capital markets and increased pressure from regulators as risks to it.
